info.name: Project X API
info.description:
Every HTTP endpoint under src/app/api in the project-x portfolio app. See docs/API.md for the full written reference this collection mirrors.

Auth: sign-in is Google/LinkedIn OAuth via Better Auth, which sets an HTTP-only session cookie — there is no bearer token to paste in. In Postman, enable Settings -> General -> "Automatically follow redirects" and turn on the cookie jar for {{baseUrl}}, sign in once through a browser against the same baseUrl, then Postman's cookie jar (Cookies link under Send, or the built-in browser) can reuse that session. Everything under the Admin folder additionally requires the signed-in account's email to be listed in ADMIN_EMAILS.

Mutating requests (POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE) are rejected unless the Origin header matches the request's own host. Every request in this collection sets Origin to {{baseUrl}} for that reason — leave it as-is even when testing against a deployed URL.

Every JSON response follows one of two shapes: {"success": true, ...} or {"success": false, "error": string, ...}. The two oldest routes (AI chat, contact) predate that convention and are called out individually below.

body.raw:
{
  "name": "Jane Doe",
  "email": "jane@example.com",
  "subject": "Let's talk",
  "message": "Hi, I saw your portfolio and wanted to reach out about a role.",
  "company": ""
}

request.description:
No auth. Rate-limited to 5/hour per IP (429 + Retry-After when exceeded). `company` is a honeypot field: real forms never fill it, so a non-empty value returns a fake 200 success without sending anything.

Constraints: name 1-100 chars, email valid + <=200 chars, subject 1-200 chars, message 10-5000 chars.

Note: this route predates the shared response-guard convention, so success is `{success:true, name}` and validation failure is `{success:false, error, fieldErrors}` (matches the common shape) but a send failure is `{error}` with no `success` key at all -- treat any non-2xx here defensively.

No auth. Rate-limited per IP (config AI_RATE_LIMIT/AI_RATE_WINDOW). `messages` is a 1..AI_MAX_HISTORY array of {role: "user"|"assistant", content: 1..AI_MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH chars}.

Success is a streamed `text/plain` body (the answer), optionally followed by a sentinel + JSON block carrying source citations, with an `X-Cache: HIT|MISS` response header. This route predates the shared guards too: every error response is `{error: string}` with no `success` key, unlike the rest of the API. 503 means GEMINI_API_KEY isn't configured; the assistant still degrades gracefully rather than crashing the page that embeds it.

No auth required to read. If a session cookie is present, `liked` reflects that viewer's own like. Rate-limited 60/min per IP. 404 if the blog has no database configured, or the post doesn't exist / isn't published.
Requires a signed-in session cookie (401 otherwise). No body. Rate-limited 30/min per user. Flips the current user's like and returns the new count.

Requires a signed-in session cookie. Body length is bounded by BLOG_COMMENT_MIN_LENGTH/MAX_LENGTH (defaults 2-2000 chars). Add `"parentId": "<comment uuid>"` to reply one level deep instead of starting a new thread.

201 on success, with `status: "visible"|"pending"` depending on the moderation policy (BLOG_COMMENT_MODERATION) and the link-count heuristic. 403 if the account is blocked (message deliberately does not say why). 404 if the post/parent doesn't exist, isn't published, or the parent is hidden.

Requires a signed-in session cookie, and only within BLOG_COMMENT_EDIT_WINDOW_MINUTES (default 15) of posting. 404 (not 403) for someone else's comment, an expired window, or a withdrawn comment -- the endpoint never reveals which.
Requires a signed-in session cookie. Soft delete (no edit window limit, unlike editing) -- the comment's spot in the thread is kept but its body is replaced with a withdrawal notice.

No auth. Rate-limited 20/5min per IP. Streams the app's latest GitHub release .apk through this origin (visitors are never redirected to github.com). 404 if the app has no configured repo; 503 if APPS_GITHUB_TOKEN isn't set; 502 on a GitHub-side failure.
Same as the latest-release download, pinned to one release tag instead of always the newest.

src/app/api/auth/[...all]/route.ts hands every /api/auth/* path to Better Auth's own Next.js handler, which owns sign-in, the OAuth callback, session lookup and sign-out under this one prefix -- this collection does not enumerate its internal sub-routes, since they're a third-party library's surface, not this app's. This one example (get-session) is the one most useful for confirming a Postman cookie jar is actually authenticated before calling anything under Admin below.

503 with {success:false, error:"Sign-in isn't available right now."} means BETTER_AUTH_SECRET / GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET aren't all set -- sign-in is entirely optional and the rest of the site is unaffected when it's off.

item.name: Admin - Posts
item.description: Every request here requires an admin session cookie (the signed-in account's email must be in ADMIN_EMAILS). A non-admin gets 404, not 401/403 -- the panel's existence is not revealed to a signed-in-but-unlisted account.

body.raw:
{
  "title": "How I profile a slow Postgres query",
  "slug": "profiling-slow-postgres-queries",
  "body": "Full post body, Markdown-free plain text.",
  "excerpt": "",
  "tags": ["postgres", "performance"]
}

request.description:
slug: 1-80 chars, lowercase, kebab-case pattern, required. body: 1-100000 chars, required. title <=200 (defaults to ""), excerpt <=400 (auto-derived from body when left empty), tags: up to 8 strings of 1-30 chars each.

201 on success. 400 with `fieldErrors` on a validation failure. 409 if the slug is already taken.

body.raw:
{
  "title": "How I profile a slow Postgres query (updated)",
  "slug": "profiling-slow-postgres-queries",
  "body": "Updated full post body.",
  "excerpt": "",
  "tags": ["postgres", "performance"]
}

request.description: Same schema and constraints as create. 404 if the id doesn't exist. 409 on a slug collision with a different post.
Cascades: deletes the post's comments and reactions, removes its cover image from Blob storage, and best-effort removes the live LinkedIn post if one was shared.

`action` is one of "publish" | "unpublish" | "pin" | "unpin".

publish's response includes `linkedIn: "shared"|"not_connected"|"skipped"|"failed"` -- publishing never fails just because the LinkedIn cross-post did.

commentary: up to 3000 chars. Left empty, LinkedIn shows the post's title instead. `synced: true` in the response means an already-live LinkedIn post was updated in place; otherwise this only takes effect on the next publish/share.

multipart/form-data, field `file`: image/*, <=4MB. Also uploads the same image to LinkedIn's asset storage (best-effort) so a future share has a thumbnail. Replacing an existing cover image clears every extra gallery photo, since the gallery is always "cover, then extras".
LinkedIn-only extra gallery photo (up to 8, on top of the cover image). Requires a cover image to already exist (400 otherwise) and LinkedIn to be connected (503 otherwise).
`index` is the photo's position in the current gallery list -- the server always re-reads the current list first, so the client never has to track or resend positions itself.
Any file type, <=4MB. Shared instead of the default article-link preview. Requires LinkedIn to be connected (503 otherwise).
`action` is "approve" (pending -> visible) or "hide" (visible -> hidden).
Unlike a reader withdrawing their own comment (soft delete), this is a hard delete and cascades to its replies. There is no undo.
`reason` <=200 chars, optional, for the admin's own reference -- never shown to the blocked user. 400 if the target id is the acting admin's own account.

item.name: Admin - Content editor
item.description: Backs /admin/content, the browser-based editor for src/content/*.json. Saving writes a real commit to GitHub, which triggers a normal deployment -- there is no separate "publish" step. Requires GITHUB_TOKEN/GITHUB_REPO to be configured (503 otherwise).

request.description: `:section` is one of profile | experience | projects | apps | skills | education | ai (404 for anything else). Returns `{data, sha}` -- `sha` is the file's current git blob hash, required by the PUT below for optimistic concurrency.

Body capped at 512KB. `data` must validate against the section's schema before any GitHub call is made (400 with `issues` otherwise). `sha` must match the file's current blob hash -- a 409 means someone else (or another tab) saved first; re-fetch with GET and reapply your change on top of theirs.
